$comment: PERMANENT Android release identity for S4 (UAT-MOB-02, Gate 4A).
This file holds PUBLIC data only: the certificate SHA-256 fingerprint, the package id and the
expected release metadata. It contains no keystore, no alias, no password and no private key, and it
must never be made to hold any of them — the keystore itself stays outside the repository.
Gate 4A moved S4 to its permanent store identity, com.sfour.s4, starting at 1.1.0 / versionCode 13.
That is a NEW Android application: it cannot update, and is not updated by, the development-era
com.securitymarketplace.mobile builds, whose records are kept below under legacyPackage.
The signer is unchanged: the same permanent S4 certificate signed every historical S4 APK and signs
com.sfour.s4. Under Google Play App Signing (Gate 4B) it is the UPLOAD key, so this is the
certificate an uploaded AAB, or a locally signed APK, must carry. The certificate Google then signs
installed copies with is recorded here as playAppSigning.appSigningCertificateSha256 once the Play
app exists — it is not known before then and must not be guessed.
Why the pin exists at all: EAS Build 8 was signed with an EAS-generated keystore instead of this one,
and nothing in the release process could see it until a device refused the update.
